title: SAMPLE: Improving Imaging Referral Quality with a Structured Checklist
authors: Alex Example; Taylor Sample | Fictional Health Sciences Teaching Unit
abstract: Background: Complete referrals support effective imaging decisions. Objective: Demonstrate a structured submission using fictional teaching data. Methods: A simulated audit compared 20 fictional referrals before and after a checklist exercise. Results: Complete referral fields increased from 12 of 20 to 18 of 20. Conclusion: This example demonstrates manuscript formatting and the review workflow. The figures are invented and must not inform clinical practice.

title: SAMPLE: Peer Learning for Health Sciences Students
authors: Jordan Demo; Casey Example | Fictional Academic Collaboration Group
abstract: Background: Peer learning may support discussion and confidence. Objective: Provide a fictional conference abstract for platform testing. Methods: Ten fictional students completed a simulated peer discussion exercise. Results: Eight reported greater confidence in this invented scenario. Conclusion: The sample is suitable for testing abstract entry, review and publication; it is not evidence of educational effectiveness.
